raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #63278. A PEFT adapter can carry LoRA weights for a layer that vLLM keeps as a plain `nn.Linear`, such as `bert.pooler.dense` in BERT models trained with `target_modules="all-linear"`. vLLM loaded these adapters and ignored those weights without a warning, so outputs differed from transformers + PEFT. vLLM now refuses such an adapter at load and names the modules, as discussed in #60211.

## Claims

- An adapter with LoRA weights on a module that vLLM cannot apply LoRA to fails to load with a `ValueError` naming the modules, for example `bert.pooler.dense` on BERT and `classifier.dense` on RoBERTa. On main these adapters load and their outputs differ from transformers + PEFT.
- On a running server, `/v1/load_lora_adapter` returns the error, the adapter is not registered, and the server stays healthy.
- Adapters whose LoRA weights all land on modules vLLM wraps load as before.
- Weights the LoRA manager already skips on purpose are still skipped: layers on another pipeline stage, layers outside `--lora-target-modules`, tower and connector layers without a PunicaWrapper, the non-gated MoE `mixer.gate`, and linear layers no LoRA layer can wrap.

## Validation

RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, fp16, `llm.llm_engine.add_lora(...)` for each adapter (the call behind `/v1/load_lora_adapter`):

| Adapter | Base model | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Shankarblr/bert-emotion-lora-adapter` (LoRA on `bert.pooler.dense`) | `bert-base-uncased`, 6 labels | loads | `ValueError` for `bert.pooler.dense` |
| Same adapter with the pooler LoRA removed | same | loads | loads |
| Fresh `all-linear` SEQ_CLS adapter with saved head, as in the #63278 repro | `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` | loads | `ValueError` for `bert.pooler.dense` |
| `query`, `value`, `dense` (PEFT also matches the pooler) | same | loads | `ValueError` for `bert.pooler.dense` |
| `query`, `value`, `dense` on the encoder only | same | loads | loads |
| `query`, `value` with saved head | same | loads | loads |
| LoRA on `classifier.dense` | `FacebookAI/roberta-base`, 3 labels | loads | `ValueError` for `classifier.dense` |
| `query`, `value` only | same | loads | loads |

The adapter fails with the existing unexpected modules error, which now lists `bert.pooler.dense (not a LoRA layer)`.

What the refused adapter costs on main: on the first 500 rows of the `dair-ai/emotion` test split, the emotion adapter reaches 94.2% accuracy with transformers + PEFT and 88.2% with vLLM main. 46 predictions change and logits differ by up to 6.71.

On `vllm serve` with the same base, `/v1/load_lora_adapter` for the emotion adapter returns 200 on main. With this PR it returns 500 with the message above, `/classify` with the adapter name returns 404, and `/health` stays 200. Passing the adapter straight to `LLM.classify` raises the same `ValueError` in the engine core, which surfaces as `EngineDeadError`, like the other adapter load errors.

Adapters on other families that must keep loading, all on this PR:

- `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` with `jeeejeee/qwen35-4b-text-only-sql-lora` and the all-linear `jeeejeee/qwen35-4b-all-linear-pokemon-lora`, with `enable_tower_connector_lora` on and off. Both load on main and on this PR, and `test_qwen35_text_lora` passes locally with its CUDA skip removed.
- `openai/gpt-oss-20b` with `jeeejeee/gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter-text2sql`, whose keys include `mlp.experts.base_layer.lora_A.weight`. It loads and answers a prompt with `SELECT count(*) FROM users`.

Tests:

```
pytest tests/lora/test_sequence_classification.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_utils.py tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py tests/lora/test_lora_checkpoints.py
94 passed, 1 skipped

pytest tests/lora/test_lora_functions.py tests/lora/test_qwen3_unembed.py tests/lora/test_lora_huggingface.py tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py tests/lora/test_qwenvl.py
11 passed, 2 skipped

pytest tests/lora/test_worker.py
1 passed

VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 pytest tests/lora/test_transformers_model.py -k "test_ilama_lora and not tp4"
1 passed
```

The skips are the TP test, which needs 2 GPUs, and the two Qwen2.5-VL tests that skip on CUDA. This card has about 14.6 GiB free, so `test_worker.py`, `test_ilama_lora` and `test_qwen35_text_lora` ran from local copies with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85` instead of the default 0.92. The new `test_lora_on_unsupported_module_is_rejected` fails on main:

```
pytest tests/lora/test_sequence_classification.py -k unsupported_module
E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE Exception
```

## Details

Root cause: `check_unexpected_modules` in `vllm/lora/lora_model.py` compares only the last part of each module name with the expected suffixes, which come from the model's `LinearBase` layers. BERT's encoder has `LinearBase` layers named `dense`, so `bert.pooler.dense` passes, although `BertPooler.dense` is a plain `nn.Linear` that `_create_lora_modules` never wraps. `activate_adapter` only reads weights for wrapped modules, so the pooler LoRA is never used. RoBERTa's `classifier.dense` takes the same path.

Change: `_create_lora_modules` records the layers it skips because `is_supported_lora_module` rejects them although their name ends in a LoRA target suffix. `check_unexpected_modules` treats LoRA weights on those layers as unexpected, so the adapter is refused while its checkpoint is read, before the LoRA model is built. It is never cached and never evicts another adapter, including on in-place reloads.

What stays skipped, and why:

- Weights for a `PPMissingLayer` or for a path through one belong to another pipeline stage, which applies them.
- Weights outside `--lora-target-modules` are excluded by the user.
- Weights without a PunicaWrapper, such as tower and connector layers when `enable_tower_connector_lora` is off, are already logged as ignored at startup.
- The non-gated MoE `mixer.gate` is a `GateLinear` and linear layers no LoRA layer can wrap are `LinearBase` too, so `is_supported_lora_module` accepts them and they keep their current behavior.
- Names that match no module of the model at all also keep their current behavior. That case, such as a text-only adapter on a multimodal wrapper with no name mapping, is what the draft #60039 covers. It raises only when no weight matches and warns on a partial match, so the pooler case would only log a warning there. The two changes do not overlap in code and can land in either order.

Once a model wraps a head linear, as #60211 does for RoBERTa's `classifier.dense`, its LoRA weights load and this check no longer fires for it.

Limits:

- The server returns 500 for this error, as it does for other `add_lora` failures.
- Pipeline and expert parallel runs were not tested, only covered by the `PPMissingLayer` and expert name handling described above.
- The new test downloads `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` and writes a small adapter in the test, so it needs no PEFT.

---

@linitra24 Yes, moved it there. `_create_lora_modules` now records the layers it skips because they are not LoRA layers but share a suffix with one, such as `bert.pooler.dense` and RoBERTa's `classifier.dense`. `check_unexpected_modules` reports LoRA weights on those layers along with the other unexpected modules, while the checkpoint is read. The separate validation pass is gone, so the wrapping rule lives only in `_create_lora_modules`. The adapters in the table are refused and accepted as before.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Could we extend the existing check_unexpected_modules check to cover this case, rather than introduce another validation pass after loading?

This would keep module compatibility validation in one place and avoid duplicating the wrapping eligibility rules in a separate validator. Would that be feasible for this fix?
Could we remove it? I don’t think this fix needs an additional documentation note.
